observation.visible_scene: A low-angle, fixed view of the corner of a modern glass-clad building. A vertical stone/concrete column runs up the corner, topped by a dark recessed notch. To the right is a large mirrored glass facade divided by a static grid of dark mullions, reflecting deep blue sky and white cumulus clouds; the angled corner panels also carry sky/cloud reflections.
visible_changes: The building structure and the mullion grid stay in identical pixel positions across all frames, indicating no camera pan/tilt/zoom and no object translation of the facade.

The reflected clouds drift slowly across the right facade: the main cloud mass that sits low-right in the early frames shifts leftward and slightly upward, and a small wispy reflection that is absent at the top-right corner in frame 1 appears there in mid/late frames and moves leftward.
Reflections on the angled corner glass panels change in step with the facade, with cloud shapes entering and leaving the narrower left-side panels as the reflected sky moves.
The blue sky tone and the dark corner notch remain constant; only the cloud patterns within the reflections change.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual sky and real cloud motion outside the frame (the reflection geometry does not by itself confirm the true wind direction or speed).
Events before t=0 and after t=3.33 s, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
The building's identity, surroundings, and whether the camera is truly hand-held or locked off.
uncertain_details: Exact speed and direction of the real clouds versus the apparent leftward drift of their reflections (reflection can invert or skew motion).
Whether any sub-pixel camera jitter exists; the mullions appear locked, so the scene is treated as a static camera with moving reflections.
